page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a chapter heading above it. Marginal notes run down the left margin: the title of the work, a note on the formal principle, a note on the final causes, and the numerals 1 to 4 beside the four causes. Running head at the top with the page number 28.

main_text.l: SEquitur doctrina Strigelii de principiis. Deus Opti-
mus Maximus cum conderet hominem, sparsit in

l.i: mentem humanam radios sive rivulos suæ lucis &
sapientiæ. Hi sive radii sive rivuli divinæ

main_text.l: sapientiæ vocantur principia, id est, notitiæ nobi-
principiorum est lumen naturale, de quo non

l.i: possumus multa dicere. Sicut enim miramur lucem
solis & stellarum & lumen oculorum, quo discernun-
tur objecta; nec tamen rationem mirandæ hujus lu-
cis, sive in stellis, sive in oculis penitus perspicimus: ita
magis mirari, quam explicare possumus formale

main_text.l: causæ finales sunt numero quatuor. Prima;

l.i: ut sint testimonia de Deo. Etsi enim multa sunt te-
stimonia de Deo in tota rerum natura: tamen praci-
pua sumuntur a mente humana, & a notitiis natu-

main_text.l: ralibus. Secunda; ut discernant nos a bestiis. Ter-
tia; ut regant hanc vitam civilem. Ex practicis e-

l.i: nim principiis extruuntur leges civiles, & omnes ho-
nestæ sententiæ de moribus. Omnes libelli gnomologici
alii, qui continent honestas de moribus sententias,
sunt rivuli deducti ex fonte principiorum practico-

main_text.l: rum. Quarta; ut gignant honestas artes, quarum

l.i: usus in vita est necessarius: ut, notitia numerorum
gignit Arithmeticam; notitia figurarum gignit Geo-

page.notes: The chapter heading and text are printed in a mix of roman and italic; italic runs were judged from the scan and may be slightly off at their edges. The numeral beside "Prima" reads as "1." but the first mark is slightly ambiguous. The long s is transcribed as plain s throughout (e.g. "caufæ" as "causæ"). Printed hyphens at line ends are kept. No catchword, signature or other furniture is visible.
